reconcile.note: Clarke ties Romans 4:19's dead-body language to Isaac's birth, then argues Genesis 25's Keturah sons are recorded out of order, born before rather than after that miraculous birth.

discrepancy.emptyNote: William Henry Burr catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: William Henry Burr, Self-Contradictions of the Bible (1860).

sides.snippet: She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
sides.verseText: She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.

sides.snippet: he didn't consider his own body, already having been worn out, (he being about a hundred years old), and the deadness of Sarah's womb.
sides.verseText: Without being weakened in faith, he didn't consider his own body, already having been worn out, (he being about a hundred years old), and the deadness of Sarah's womb.
